_comment: A profile is the answers you would otherwise retype into every script.json: which
backend renders, which voice reads, which palette, how much you are willing to spend.
Precedence, narrowest wins:  script.json  >  --flags  >  profile  >  .env  >  defaults.
A profile never overrides something the script states explicitly.
name: business
description: Client or company work. Consistent brand, paid voice, a budget that someone signs off.
_backend: Still html by default, on purpose. The api backend bills per second of video: Veo 3.1
at $0.40/s means a 60-second video is $24, and a week of dailies is $168. Switch to
api for one hero video, not for the daily queue — and set costCeilingUsd first.
_voice: A paid provider is the honest default here: client work is where a synthetic-sounding read costs more than the API bill. Set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and TTS_VOICE_ID in .env — never here, this file is committed.
_theme: A key from video-templates/theme-map.json. One value repaints every template, which is how a queue of videos ends up looking like one brand rather than fourteen.
_brand: Fill these once. An empty field drops its slot instead of filling it with a placeholder — the templates used to default to the upstream author's channel, and a video published with someone else's URL is worse than one with no URL.
_costCeilingUsd: Per render. The api backend prints its estimate and refuses to start above this,
before spending anything. 25 is roughly one 60-second Veo 3.1 clip — high enough to
let a deliberate hero video through, low enough that a queue misconfigured to use
api stops on the first item instead of the fiftieth.
